database_summary: Relational catalog of a digital media store (Chinook-like). Core entities: Artists, Albums, Tracks, Genres, MediaTypes, Customers, Employees, Playlists. Transactional/sales facts: Invoices and InvoiceLines. Bridge table: PlaylistTrack linking Playlist and Track. Row counts: small-to-moderate (tracks ~3503, invoice lines 2240, playlisttrack 8715). Primary keys and FKs are explicit; no temporal history tables beyond invoice timestamps. Reasonable for analytical queries (sales, catalog, customer support).

accepted.name: track_with_catalog_info
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  Track.TrackId AS TrackId,
  Track.Name AS Name,
  Track.AlbumId AS AlbumId,
  Album.Title AS Title,
  Album.ArtistId AS ArtistId,
  Artist.Name AS Name_Artist,
  Track.MediaTypeId AS MediaTypeId,
  MediaType.Name AS Name_MediaType,
  Track.GenreId AS GenreId,
  Genre.Name AS Name_Genre,
  Track.Composer AS Composer,
  Track.Milliseconds AS Milliseconds,
  Track.Bytes AS Bytes,
  Track.UnitPrice AS UnitPrice
FROM Track
LEFT JOIN Album ON Track.AlbumId = Album.AlbumId
LEFT JOIN Artist ON Album.ArtistId = Artist.ArtistId
LEFT JOIN Genre ON Track.GenreId = Genre.GenreId
LEFT JOIN MediaType ON Track.MediaTypeId = MediaType.MediaTypeId
accepted.description: One row per Track enriched with its Album, Artist, Genre, and MediaType attributes. Useful when queries need a denormalized view of a track's catalog metadata for filtering, grouping, or joining to sales. | Use for: list tracks with artist/album/genre for browsing or export; aggregate track measures (duration, size, price) by artist/genre/media type; filter tracks by artist name, genre name, or media type

accepted.name: invoice_line_with_context
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  InvoiceLine.InvoiceLineId AS InvoiceLineId,
  InvoiceLine.InvoiceId AS InvoiceId,
  Invoice.InvoiceDate AS InvoiceDate,
  Invoice.CustomerId AS CustomerId,
  Customer.FirstName AS FirstName,
  Customer.LastName AS LastName,
  Customer.Country AS Country,
  InvoiceLine.TrackId AS TrackId,
  Track.Name AS Name_Track,
  Track.AlbumId AS AlbumId,
  Album.Title AS Title,
  Album.ArtistId AS ArtistId,
  Artist.Name AS Name_Artist,
  InvoiceLine.UnitPrice AS UnitPrice,
  InvoiceLine.Quantity AS Quantity
FROM InvoiceLine
JOIN Invoice ON InvoiceLine.InvoiceId = Invoice.InvoiceId
LEFT JOIN Customer ON Invoice.CustomerId = Customer.CustomerId
LEFT JOIN Track ON InvoiceLine.TrackId = Track.TrackId
LEFT JOIN Album ON Track.AlbumId = Album.AlbumId
LEFT JOIN Artist ON Album.ArtistId = Artist.ArtistId
accepted.description: One row per InvoiceLine enriched with its Invoice header, Customer, Track, Album, and Artist context. Useful for sales-level analyses that need both line-item details and customer or catalog attributes. | Use for: compute revenue, units sold per track/artist/customer; customer purchase history with track/artist details; verify invoice totals against sum of invoice lines

accepted.name: album_artist_aggregate
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  Album.AlbumId AS AlbumId,
  Album.Title AS Title,
  Album.ArtistId AS ArtistId,
  COUNT(Track.TrackId) AS track_count,
  SUM(Track.Milliseconds) AS total_milliseconds,
  SUM(Track.Bytes) AS total_bytes,
  AVG(Track.UnitPrice) AS avg_track_unitprice
FROM Album
LEFT JOIN Track ON Track.AlbumId = Album.AlbumId
GROUP BY Album.AlbumId, Album.Title, Album.ArtistId
accepted.description: One row per Album with counts and aggregates of its Tracks (number of tracks, total duration, total bytes, average track price). Useful for album-level summaries and comparative analytics across artists or genres. | Use for: rank or compare albums by number of tracks or total duration; join album aggregates to artist-level summaries; identify albums with unusually high/low average price

accepted.name: customer_invoice_aggregate
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  Customer.CustomerId AS CustomerId,
  Customer.FirstName AS FirstName,
  Customer.LastName AS LastName,
  Customer.Country AS Country,
  COUNT(Invoice.InvoiceId) AS invoice_count,
  SUM(Invoice.Total) AS total_revenue,
  AVG(Invoice.Total) AS avg_invoice_total,
  MAX(Invoice.InvoiceDate) AS last_invoice_date
FROM Customer
LEFT JOIN Invoice ON Invoice.CustomerId = Customer.CustomerId
GROUP BY Customer.CustomerId, Customer.FirstName, Customer.LastName, Customer.Country
accepted.description: One row per Customer with aggregated invoice measures: number of invoices, total revenue, average invoice value, last invoice date. Useful for customer lifetime value, segmentation, and support reporting. | Use for: compute customer lifetime value and recency; segment customers by purchase frequency or revenue; identify inactive customers (invoice_count = 0)

accepted.name: playlist_track_counts
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  Playlist.PlaylistId AS PlaylistId,
  Playlist.Name AS Name,
  COUNT(PlaylistTrack.TrackId) AS track_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT Track.AlbumId) AS distinct_album_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT Album.ArtistId) AS distinct_artist_count
FROM Playlist
LEFT JOIN PlaylistTrack ON Playlist.PlaylistId = PlaylistTrack.PlaylistId
LEFT JOIN Track ON PlaylistTrack.TrackId = Track.TrackId
LEFT JOIN Album ON Track.AlbumId = Album.AlbumId
GROUP BY Playlist.PlaylistId, Playlist.Name
accepted.description: One row per Playlist with number of tracks and distinct artists represented. Useful for playlist summaries, quality checks, and recommendations. | Use for: find largest playlists by number of tracks; measure diversity of playlists by artist or album counts; filter playlists by minimum track_count or artist diversity

accepted.name: invoices_with_line_totals
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  InvoiceLine.InvoiceLineId AS InvoiceLineId,
  InvoiceLine.InvoiceId AS InvoiceId,
  InvoiceLine.TrackId AS TrackId,
  InvoiceLine.UnitPrice AS UnitPrice,
  InvoiceLine.Quantity AS Quantity,
  (InvoiceLine.UnitPrice * InvoiceLine.Quantity) AS line_total,
  (InvoiceLine.UnitPrice IS NULL) AS unitprice_missing
FROM InvoiceLine
accepted.description: InvoiceLine rows with a deterministic computed line_total (UnitPrice * Quantity) and a flag indicating if UnitPrice is NULL. Useful to ensure consistent line-level revenue calculations when computing invoice sums or diagnosing missing prices. | Use for: recompute invoice totals from invoice lines; identify invoice lines with missing pricing; aggregate revenue per track or invoice using line_total

accepted.name: customer_full_name
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  Customer.CustomerId AS CustomerId,
  Customer.FirstName AS FirstName,
  Customer.LastName AS LastName,
  (Customer.FirstName || ' ' || Customer.LastName) AS full_name,
  Customer.Company AS Company,
  Customer.Email AS Email,
  Customer.Country AS Country,
  Customer.SupportRepId AS SupportRepId
FROM Customer
accepted.description: One row per Customer with a computed full_name and canonical contact fields for easier display and grouping. Useful for UI exports and grouping by customer identity. | Use for: display customer lists with full name; group or filter customers by country or support rep; export customer contact lists

accepted.name: track_sales_summary
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  Track.TrackId AS TrackId,
  Track.Name AS Name,
  COUNT(InvoiceLine.InvoiceLineId) AS units_sold,
  SUM(InvoiceLine.UnitPrice * InvoiceLine.Quantity) AS revenue,
  COUNT(DISTINCT InvoiceLine.InvoiceId) AS invoice_count
FROM Track
LEFT JOIN InvoiceLine ON InvoiceLine.TrackId = Track.TrackId
GROUP BY Track.TrackId, Track.Name
accepted.description: One row per Track with aggregated sales metrics: units_sold, revenue (sum of line_total), and number_of_invoices. Useful for top-selling track reports, revenue attribution, and inventoryless sales analytics. | Use for: list top-selling tracks by revenue or units; compare track sales across genres or albums (joinable); identify tracks with many invoices but low units (anomalies)

accepted.name: artist_sales_aggregate
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  Artist.ArtistId AS ArtistId,
  Artist.Name AS Name,
  COUNT(InvoiceLine.InvoiceLineId) AS units_sold,
  SUM(InvoiceLine.UnitPrice * InvoiceLine.Quantity) AS revenue
FROM Artist
LEFT JOIN Album ON Album.ArtistId = Artist.ArtistId
LEFT JOIN Track ON Track.AlbumId = Album.AlbumId
LEFT JOIN InvoiceLine ON InvoiceLine.TrackId = Track.TrackId
GROUP BY Artist.ArtistId, Artist.Name
accepted.description: One row per Artist aggregating sales through joins from Artist -> Album -> Track -> InvoiceLine -> Invoice. Produces total revenue and total units sold per artist. Useful for artist-level royalty calculations and leaderboard reports. | Use for: rank artists by revenue or units sold; compute artist share of total sales; identify artists with many tracks but low sales

accepted.name: latest_invoice_per_customer
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  Invoice.CustomerId AS CustomerId,
  Invoice.InvoiceId AS InvoiceId,
  Invoice.InvoiceDate AS InvoiceDate,
  Invoice.BillingCountry AS BillingCountry,
  Invoice.Total AS Total
FROM Invoice
JOIN (
  SELECT CustomerId, MAX(InvoiceDate) AS max_invoice_date
  FROM Invoice
  GROUP BY CustomerId
) AS latest ON Invoice.CustomerId = latest.CustomerId AND Invoice.InvoiceDate = latest.max_invoice_date
accepted.description: One row per Customer containing their most recent Invoice (by InvoiceDate). Useful for recency calculations, churn detection, and identifying last purchase details. | Use for: compute recency per customer; join last invoice to customer records for outreach; analyze last purchase amounts by customer segments
